note: Moor: two or three lone rowans and wind-bent hawthorns, far apart (specimen trees, about 1 per 40 m); the mounds, cairns and stones stay.
Stone shrine: a ring of old yews round the stones (5 or 6), a holly; the open middle stays open.
Log pile: young birches and aspens taking over between the logs, in two loose clumps; the logs and snags stay.
Ravine: Scots pines, birches and a rowan clinging to its rims, leaning out (edges only); the rocks and spires stay.
Meadow: one great field oak and a few lone hawthorns (specimen trees); the grass stays open for the flowers.
Grassland: two hedgerow islands of hawthorn and crab apple (clumps of 2 or 3); open turf between.
Heath: a couple of lone Scots pines and a clump of birch on the heather (scattered, sparse).
Wetland: pollard willows and alders by the pools, in clumps, into the middle as well as round the edge.
Stream: alders and willows lining the banks, a row along the water (denser than today's).
Fen: alder carr, low wet clumps of alder with a willow, among the pools (2 or 3 clumps an area).
Heronry: one great heron tree (a tall elm, its nests on the set piece's kind), willows round the mere.
Beaver pond: aspens and birches round the pond, some leaning where the beavers have gnawed them (edges).
